model_output.verdict: A marketing coordinator with a substantial email list, but no work dated after March 2024.
write_up: Your resume points to Marketing Coordinator work across email, events and social media at Juniper Outdoor Co. and Fernwood Coffee Roasters. The work is easy to follow, but a recruiter has to account for the time since your last dated role before moving forward.

The weekly email calendar is your strongest line: it names the work, its frequency and the list of 120,000 subscribers. Your headline fits the jobs, and Experience is in the right place above Education. Nothing on the resume explains the time after March 2024.

Let's start with what you've done since Juniper, if there's something you can add honestly. Then give the social posts and earlier tasting events a little more detail about your part. You can leave the trade show line alone: four events a year tells a recruiter something useful.

cards.line: Nothing is dated after March 2024.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what you've done since the Juniper role. If you were caring for a family member, taking a career break, studying, volunteering or doing real freelance work, you can name that honestly. A referral may matter more when the time isn't explained.

cards.cannot_tell: The platforms are clear, but a recruiter can't tell how often you posted or what the posts supported. That would show more of your social media work.
